replication.target_description: Primary replication report, undergraduate scratch-card experiment; supplied p. 9 and broad description encompass Card 2 outcome-by-condition interaction, final-outcome between-condition t-test, urge/purchase correlations, and condition/purchase-status ANOVA. No unique critical test is identified.

n.exclusions: One participant excluded from all analyses for procedural error; three removed from all urge analyses, plus three from card 1 urge analyses for incorrect numbers of ratings. Purchasing and urge analytic samples differ.
n.location: Text/PDF page 8, Purchasing Behaviour and Urge to Continue Gambling / Analytical Strategy
n.quote:
Of the entire sample (N = 137), only 18% of participants chose to purchase an additional
scratch card with their winnings (n = 25). In the loss condition (n = 68), 21% (n = 14) of
participants purchased an additional card, and in the near-miss condition (n = 69), 16%
(n = 11) of participants decided to purchase. ... Three participants were removed from all urge analyses and three
were removed from card 1 urge analyses for giving an incorrect number of ratings per card.

reported_success.quote:
registered pattern of urge findings was replicated, with wins and near-misses leading to
increases in the urge to continue gambling compared to regular losing outcomes. However,
we did not replicate our previously reported association between urge ratings at the final
outcome and the decision to purchase additional cards in the near-miss condition.
